turns.user_message: If a train leaves at 9:00 going 80 km/h and another leaves at 10:00 from the same station going 120 km/h, when does the second catch up?

steps.reasoning:
We need to answer a word problem. No data needed. Compute when second catches up.

First train leaves at 9:00 at {{int:64:96}} km/h. At 10:00, it has been traveling 1 hour, distance = {{int:64:96}} km. Second train starts at 10:00 at {{int:96:144}} km/h. We need time t after 10:00 when distances equal.

Let t be hours after 10:00. Distance of second = {{int:96:144}} t. Distance of first = {{int:64:96}} km (head start) + {{int:64:96}} t (since continues). Set equal: {{int:96:144}} t = {{int:64:96}} + {{int:64:96}} t => 120t - 80t = {{int:64:96}} => 40t = {{int:64:96}} => t = 2 hours.

Thus second catches up at 10:00 + 2h = 12:00 (noon). Answer.
steps.text:
The first train has a 1‑hour head start.  
- At 10:00 it is \({{int:64:96}} \text{ km}\) ahead ( \({{int:64:96}} \text{ km/h} \times 1\text{ h}\) ).  
- From 10:00 onward both trains travel, so let \(t\) be the hours after 10:00 when they meet.

Set their distances equal:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{Second train distance} &= 120t \\
\text{First train distance} &= {{int:64:96}} + 80t
\end{aligned}
\]

\[
120t = {{int:64:96}} + 80t \;\Longrightarrow\; 40t = {{int:64:96}} \;\Longrightarrow\; t = 2 \text{ hours}
\]

So the second train catches up **2 hours after 10:00**, i.e., at **12:00 PM**.
